title: 2026 UK ETS CCS offshore-regulator consultation QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines
UK ETS: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines (accessible webpage)

facts.source_fact: The Authority considered limiting a cross-boundary CCS pipeline to at most two regulators and two permits.
Offshore Option 1 would keep the onshore regulator responsible until the offshore storage site.
Offshore Option 1 could result in one permit for the whole pipeline to the storage site.
facts.expected_handling: Do not present as current law.

facts.source_fact: Under Offshore Option 1 OPRED would still regulate the storage site in specified UK continental shelf or English territorial-sea cases.
Offshore Option 2 would make OPRED the sole regulator for the offshore pipeline portion.
Under Offshore Option 2 there would be one onshore regulator and OPRED offshore.
The consultation considers the last onshore metering point as the transfer point to OPRED under Option 2.
The proposals are not intended to widen regulator jurisdiction for unrelated regulatory functions.
The consultation compares options rather than announcing a selected final model.
Final implementation depends on a later Authority policy decision and legal change where required.
